transcript: Last night, I saw Patriots on Broadway. This play, transferring from the West End, follows Russian business oligarch Boris Berezovsky and his help in the election of and subsequent fallout with Vladimir Putin. Now, historical plays tend to be very hit or miss for me. On one hand, they can be very interesting and illuminate aspects of human psychology in the process of examining events and figures retrospectively. Other times, they can be depressing or too close for comfort. This play I think is both. I definitely found it educational as I'm admittedly not as educated in global politics as I should be. It’s also just an interesting story of allyship and loyalty, corruption and politics, and like I mentioned earlier, human behavior. But it was also very grim. Honestly, I don't know how many more stories we need to be telling about greedy white men making shady deals and playing chess with the lives of regular people for their own personal gain. But this production, however, was really well done. The writing is strong, the direction is captivating, and particularly Michael Stuhlbarg’s performance as Boris I thought was really phenomenal. But still, with none of the characters being likable in my opinion and the play being about two and a half hours long, I don't think this will hold everyone's attention. I think if the subject matter interests you I would definitely recommend it and if it doesn't then I'd maybe recommend it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
